name: Archive mechanism selection
problem: AppCDS and the Leyden AOT cache need different JVM flags, and which one a JDK supports depends on its feature release. The JDK that runs the tool is not always the JDK that runs the application.
how: The tool first detects the target JDK from an explicit Java home, JAVA_HOME or the running JVM. It then resolves the user request (auto, appcds or aot) to one strategy. Auto means AOT on JDK 25 or later and AppCDS before that. The strategy supplies the training flag and the runtime flag.

name: Archive-ready application layout
problem: CDS and AOT archives can only reference classes that sit in ordinary JAR files on the classpath. A Spring Boot fat JAR keeps its classes and libraries in nested JARs, so an archive trained on it would hold almost nothing.
how: The tool extracts a Spring Boot JAR with the target JDK into a launcher JAR plus a lib/ directory, then launches that JAR. Other executable JARs already have the right shape and are used unchanged. The resulting runnable JAR is what training and, later, the manifest describe.

name: Training run lifecycle
problem: A server does not exit by itself, but a CDS or AOT archive is written only by a JVM that exits normally. A run must therefore be stopped at the right time, in the right way, and its result must be checked.
how: The tool starts the application with the recording flag, lets a ReadyCondition decide when startup is complete, sends SIGTERM, waits for the JVM to finish writing, then accepts the run only when the exit code is right and a non-empty archive exists. Any failed run leaves no archive.

title: A bad cache never stops an application
rule: A bad or missing cache archive must never stop an application from starting. Never pass -Xshare:on or any flag that makes the JVM fail on an archive mismatch.
why: The archive is an optimisation. A stale archive in a pod would otherwise turn a slow start into an outage.

name: Ignore-not-fail archive fallback
problem: A startup cache that is stale or mismatched must not take an application down
how: Runs use the JVM default -Xshare:auto: a mismatched archive is ignored whole and the application starts uncached; -Xshare:on is never used

name: Same-moment startup measurement
problem: Startup comparisons between variants are meaningless unless every variant is stopped at the same definition of started
how: bench reuses the exit mode's ready condition, runs fresh JVMs, discards a warm-up run and reports medians

name: Archive store
problem: Pods need a trained archive that was produced once elsewhere, and a bad or missing fetch must not stop startup
how: A fingerprint-keyed store with put/get/exists; OCI registry artifacts tagged by fingerprint and verified by SHA-256 digest

name: Archive store
problem: Pods need a trained archive produced once elsewhere, and a bad or missing fetch must not stop startup
how: A fingerprint-keyed store with put/get/exists; OCI artifacts tagged fp-<hex> and verified by content digest; separate pull and push credentials delivered to pods

name: Training trigger
problem: Replicas start together and all find no archive, but only one trainer should run
how: A Job named by the fingerprint is created by a Helm hook; Kubernetes rejects duplicate names, and the Job exits early if the store already has the archive

name: Training trigger
problem: Replicas start together and all find no archive, but only one trainer should run, and trainer failure must not affect releases
how: A non-hook CronJob computes the fingerprint in the image, checks the store, takes a fingerprint-named Lease, trains, uploads and exits 0 on any failure

title: Verify before use
rule: An archive obtained from a store is digest-checked before the JVM can load it. A size or digest mismatch discards the download and means no archive (§1), never a partial or unverified file.
why: A truncated or tampered archive handed to the JVM can crash it or run unintended code. Verification keeps a bad store or network from becoming an outage or a code-execution path.

name: Archive store
problem: Pods need a trained archive produced once elsewhere, and a bad or missing fetch must not stop startup
how: A fingerprint-keyed store with put/get/exists; OCI artifacts tagged fp-<hex>, verified by content digest while streaming; separate pull and push credentials from a Docker-config file

title: Startup helpers fail open
rule: Every component on the pod start path (fetch, run, wrapper scripts) exits 0 or falls back to a plain JVM start on any cache-related problem, and never leaves state that points at a stale archive. Only an explicit --strict mode may fail.
why: An init container that exits non-zero keeps the pod from starting at all, so an optimisation failure would become an outage. Stale flags would silently apply the wrong archive.

name: Fetch fallback chain
problem: Each pod must use a matching archive if one exists, and must still start if none does
how: Candidates ordered AOT then AppCDS; first verified hit writes archive, manifest and a flags file; any miss or error clears flags and exits 0

name: Archive launch guard
problem: A fetched archive must only be used by a launch it fits, and the JVM silently ignores it otherwise
how: run recomputes the live manifest from the java command, compares fingerprint inputs and JAR modification times, and adds the archive flag only on a full match

name: Tools image
problem: The cache tool must see the application's own JDK and JAR files, but should be shipped once
how: A JDK-free busybox image carries the jar, launcher and wrapper; it is copied into or baked into the application image and runs there

name: Training lease
problem: Several trainers can start at once, or one can crash mid-run, and training the same fingerprint twice wastes minutes
how: A Lease named after the fingerprint is created atomically; an unrenewed one expires and is taken over with a resourceVersion-checked update; the holder renews while training and deletes it when done

name: Trainer CronJob
problem: An archive must be produced in the real cluster without ever blocking a release or an application start
how: A CronJob in the application image runs train on a schedule; it is idempotent (the store check and the lease) and reports its outcome

name: Offline workload injection
problem: Teams want the cache on existing Deployments without hand-editing every pod template, and without running a cluster-side injector
how: A pure transformation of the rendered YAML: opted-in Deployments are wrapped and their trainer resources emitted in the same stream; a versioned marker stores the original launch so reinjection is deterministic and disabling restores it; checksums refuse to overwrite edited generated resources; the whole stream is rejected on any error

title: No cloud SDKs in the core
rule: warmup-core has no runtime dependencies; cloud integrations are small hand-written clients over java.net.http behind RegistryAuth
why: The tool runs on every pod start and ships as one shaded jar; an SDK adds size, supply-chain surface and class loading to a startup optimiser

name: Image-volume tools delivery
problem: Sequential tools installation and archive fetching can cancel startup savings, while inline registry credentials would be exposed to application code.
how: A read-only image volume provides the tools. The launcher fetches inline without a pull secret; with a pull secret a separate init container mounts the credential and populates the shared cache.

name: Archive launch guard
problem: A fetched archive must fit the JVM and application that will use it; mismatches must remain a safe cache miss.
how: The launch guard compares a live fingerprint with the manifest before adding an archive flag. Measurements on the Spring Boot example show that SoftMaxHeapSize can change without invalidating class reuse, so it is excluded. Maximum and initial heap, collector, RAM percentage and pointer-layout flags remain conservative inputs because large heaps and some collector changes can alter archive compatibility. A missing profile still starts uncached; automatic selection for heap sizes derived from cgroup limits is not implemented.
